local_runner.machine_revoke_description: This removes the machine from your account, revokes every Agent mount, and stops active calls.
local_runner.add_guide_description: Set up a macOS or Linux computer so agents can use its local files and tools. Runner runs in the background to provide the connection.
local_runner.install_step_description: The one-time command installs the Multica CLI and opens browser pairing. It starts Runner automatically after browser approval and keeps it running in the background. Pairing the machine does not enable it for an agent; select the machine in that agent's execution settings.
local_runner.mcp_step_description: Add each local stdio or HTTP MCP service under mcpServers in this file. Configure exactly one of command or url per service. The built-in local_machine service starts with Runner and does not belong in this file.
local_runner.mcp_restart_hint: After changing mcp.json, stop and start Runner so it reloads and reports the complete service list. Commands, environment variables, headers, and credentials remain on this machine.
local_runner.lifecycle_step_description: Runner normally stays in the background. Use these commands after installation or whenever you change its MCP configuration.
local_runner.file_access_description: On first install, Runner uses your Desktop by default. Run the command below with an existing absolute path to replace the configured directories; repeat --directory in the same command to allow more than one. A running Runner restarts automatically. These directories constrain local_machine file tools and the starting directory for Shell, but Shell still has your local user permissions.
local_runner.install_command_description: Run this one-time command on the macOS or Linux machine, then approve the browser prompt. It installs the Multica CLI, pairs the machine, and starts Runner automatically in the background.
local_runner.title: My Computer
local_runner.description: Review connected computers, which agents can use them, and the local folders you have made available.
local_runner.security_warning: Runner Shell commands use the local operating-system user's full permissions; local file access directories do not restrict the Shell. Anyone allowed to run a bound agent may trigger that machine.
local_runner.machines_description: Machines are grouped by their stable machine ID. Each agent binding keeps its own connection state and local file access directories.
local_runner.load_failed: Couldn't load your connected computers. The list may be incomplete until this succeeds.
local_runner.empty_description: Computers you connect from an agent's My Computer settings will appear here.
local_runner.reconnect_failed_toast: Couldn't create a Runner reconnect command
local_runner.disconnect_description: This stops only this agent binding and its active calls. The machine stays online while another connected agent still uses it.
local_runner.revoke_description: This permanently deletes this agent binding and stops its active calls. Other bindings on the machine are not changed.
local_runner.reconnect_command_description: Run this command on the same machine. It installs the current Runner version and restores only this agent binding without another browser authorization.
local_runner.reconnect_command_expiry: The command contains a one-time credential that expires in 10 minutes. Do not share it.

hosted_sites.title: Hosted websites
hosted_sites.description: Websites hosted by your account through Multica. This account-wide list is the same in every workspace.
hosted_sites.list_description: Open a website, copy its public link to share it, or remove it from public access.
hosted_sites.empty_description: Websites uploaded through the Multica MCP will appear here.
hosted_sites.delete_description: This website's public link will stop working immediately. Stored files are retained for audit and recovery.

workspace_access.permission_description: Applies only to this workspace. DSH configuration permits plugin uploads, agent plugin configuration, and Profile preparation/status. All permissions also includes other workspace operations.
workspace_access.title: DTA Access
workspace_access.description: Issue workspace-bound credentials for DTA. External operators use DTA only and do not receive a Multica account or personal API token.
workspace_access.owner_only: Only workspace owners can manage DTA access.
workspace_access.tokens_description: Each token represents a separate service identity in this workspace. Select all permissions or DSH configuration only, set its expiry, and revoke it at any time.
workspace_access.revoke_confirm: Revoke this DTA access key? DTA requests using it will fail immediately.
workspace_access.delete_confirm: Permanently delete this revoked token record? Its service member, agents, and history will remain.
workspace_access.member_permissions_description: This token has the same access as a standard workspace member. It can manage its own agents, tasks, traces, schedules, bindings, and stable private runtimes. It cannot manage members or workspace settings, create public managed runtimes, or administer stable releases.
workspace_access.regenerate_warning: The current key will stop working immediately. Configure the newly generated key in DTA after you save it.
workspace_access.expiry_description: All DTA requests using this token fail immediately after it expires. You can edit the expiry or regenerate the key with a new expiry.
workspace_access.permanent_warning: A token with no expiry remains usable until it is revoked. Use an expiring token when possible.
workspace_access.secret_title: Save this DTA access key now
workspace_access.secret_warning: This key is shown only once. Send it only through your approved secret-delivery channel; it cannot be recovered later.
workspace_access.secret_confirm: I have copied and stored this key safely

repository_settings.description: Manage workspace repositories, access identities, and collaboration features.
repository_settings.collaboration_description: GitHub collaboration features for task and pull request linking and commit attribution.

git_repo.description: Workspace identities for importing Agents and skills and reading publication revisions. Access uses the connected identity’s repository permissions.
